{{ElectionsOH}}
The '''2010 Ohio State Auditor election''' was held on November 2, 2010, to elect the [[Ohio State Auditor]], concurrently with elections to the [[2010 United States Senate election in Ohio|United States Senate]], [[2010 United States House of Representatives elections in Ohio|U.S. House of Representatives]], [[2010 Ohio gubernatorial election|governor]], and other [[2010 Ohio elections|state]] and [[2010 United States elections#Local elections|local]] elections. Primary elections were held on May 4, 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 Elections Results |url=https://www.ohiosos.gov/elections/election-results-and-data/2010-elections-results/ |access-date=November 3, 2025 |website=Ohio Secretary of State}}</ref>

Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] state auditor [[Mary Taylor (Ohio politician)|Mary Taylor]] originally announced she would seek re-election, but instead was [[2010 Ohio gubernatorial election|the successful]] Republican nominee for lieutenant governor after being picked by [[John Kasich]] as his running mate in January 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 15, 2009 |title=Taylor to seek re-election, not Senate seat |url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/news/2009/05/15/taylor-to-seek-re-election/23356632007/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=November 3, 2025 |website=The Columbus Dispatch |quote=State Auditor Mary Taylor has decided to run for re-election and forgo a bid for the U.S. Senate in 2010.}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=January 12, 2010 |title=Ohio Auditor Mary Taylor won't seek re-election, instead will run for lieutenant governor |url=https://www.cleveland.com/open/2010/01/ohio_auditor_mary_taylor_to_se.html |access-date=November 3, 2025 |website=The Plain Dealer}}</ref> [[Delaware County, Ohio|Delaware County]] prosecutor [[Dave Yost]] won the Republican primary against state representative [[Seth Morgan (politician)|Seth Morgan]], and [[Hamilton County, Ohio|Hamilton County]] commissioner [[David Pepper (politician)|David Pepper]] won the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] primary unopposed.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 5, 2010 |title=Republican primary for state auditor |url=https://www.wcbe.org/news/2010-05-05/republican-primary-for-state-auditor |access-date=November 3, 2025 |website=WCBE 90.5 FM}}</ref> Yost would go on to win the general election.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 3, 2010 |title=GOP's Yost to become Ohio's next state auditor |url=https://www.cantonrep.com/story/news/state/2010/11/03/gop-s-yost-to-become/42550133007/ |access-date=November 3, 2025 |website=The Canton Repository}}</ref>

== Republican primary ==
=== Candidates ===
==== Nominee ====
* [[Dave Yost]], prosecutor of [[Delaware County, Ohio|Delaware County]] and former auditor of Delaware County (1999–2003)<ref>{{Cite web |last=Naymik |first=Mark |date=January 25, 2010 |title=Delaware County Prosecutor David Yost leaves Ohio attorney general race for auditor's race |url=https://www.cleveland.com/naymik/2010/01/delaware_county_prosecutor_dav.html |access-date=November 3, 2025 |website=The Plain Dealer}}</ref>

==== Eliminated in primary ====
* [[Seth Morgan (politician)|Seth Morgan]], state representative from the 36th district (2009–present)<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 20, 2010 |title=Republican state Rep. Morgan running for auditor |url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/news/2010/01/21/republican-state-rep-morgan-running/23594815007/ |access-date=November 3, 2025 |website=The Columbus Dispatch}}</ref>

==== Withdrew ====
* [[Mary Taylor (Ohio politician)|Mary Taylor]], incumbent state auditor (2007–present) and former state representative from the 43rd district (2003–2006) ''([[2010 Ohio gubernatorial election|ran for lieutenant governor]])''<ref name=":0" />
